minutes.headline: Select Board put the police mental-health co-response, farm bylaw and four planning articles on the Nov 14 warrant.
minutes.summary: The board heard public complaints about the tax investigation team and an open meeting law finding. It took up the police chief's co-response clinician proposal and several Special Town Meeting warrant articles, and approved Boys and Girls Club events. It also took routine appointments, a town manager's report, a bond anticipation note and committee reports.

public_comment.topic: State open meeting law determination against the tax investigation team; requested electronic copies of team communications within 10 working days.
Rebutted the member's response; says no inaccuracies were identified and meetings of any two team members would violate the law.
Asked that the dump be called the sanitary landfill, thanked town staff and volunteers, supported a look at the pay structure and urged civility.

budget_items.topic: Opioid relief funds for co-response clinician
budget_items.what_was_said: Chief requested opioid settlement funds for a full-year clinician through Open Sky, split with Lancaster, which would reimburse Lunenburg as host.
The department is applying for a rolling state grant and would return opioid funds if the grant covers the first year.
One bid received far exceeds the available capital funds, so the project is dropped and the funds will be reappropriated later.
One bid for two trucks matches the ARPA commitment; old trucks go to municibid.

budget_items.topic: Community Compact best practices grant applications
budget_items.what_was_said: The town applied for financial management policies and bridge/culvert asset management plan funding.
Note on the ladder truck and former property, second to last year of payment, one year term.
A member said neighboring towns pay the clerk much more and urged review; the clerk is not in the salary plan and is set at town meeting.
A consultant fee would allow solar on the old dump at no added municipal cost.
A one-time bonus was mentioned in a joking aside.

Open meeting law determination response/appeal to be added to next week's agenda; 21-day appeal period.
Town manager to give detailed update on recruitment for open positions at the Oct 10 meeting.
Board agreed to move the water supply protection article earlier in the warrant order.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted to include a police mental-health co-response article in the Special Town Meeting warrant.
The board added the farm bylaw and articles on common driveways, solar canopies and water supply protection, and referred the planning articles to the Planning Board for hearing.
The animal bylaw was pulled from the special town meeting and deferred to spring; the board then voted unanimously to include all other draft articles.
The police chief proposed opioid settlement funds for a full-year co-response clinician, with a state grant application pending that could replace them.
The board signed a one-year bond anticipation note, and a public speaker challenged the board over an open meeting law finding against the tax investigation team.

why_it_matters: The articles now on the warrant are the ones residents will be asked to vote on at the Special Town Meeting, including a co-response clinician that could draw on opioid settlement money rather than the tax levy.
The bond anticipation note is short-term borrowing that comes back for renewal, and the open meeting law finding bears on how the town's tax investigation work is conducted in public.
watch_next: The Oct 10 meeting, where the town manager is to give a detailed update on recruitment for open positions.
Next week's agenda, which is to carry the open meeting law determination response or appeal; the minutes note a 21-day appeal period.
